### LOW: Registration docs now say the coordinator no longer verifies file hashes; the model\-integrity threats are not updated
[docs/operations/model\-migration\.md:142](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/8070ef88f7608917158a2b449f644134ea42c83d/docs/operations/model-migration.md#L142) · T-012, T-027

The head text of \`docs/operations/model\-migration\.md\` \(lines 142\-145\) now says \`HandleRegisterModel\` only validates manifest identity and inventory and checks listed file sizes\. It adds that 'Providers verify the actual file hashes when downloading\.' The base text \(lines 137\-138\) said the coordinator verified every listed file's existence, size and hash\. If this reflects a real backend change, publication\-time integrity checking has moved from the trusted coordinator to adversarial providers\. A bad or tampered CDN/R2 object, or a manifest that does not match the files, would then be caught only on provider devices\. A malicious provider \(ADV\-001\) can skip that check and serve substituted weights \(T\-012, T\-027, A\-004\)\. The new step 1 text also lets operators reuse already\-published files without re\-upload\. Nothing in the supplied threat model records that the coordinator stopped checking hashes\. Update the weight\-substitution threats and mitigations to state the new verification point\. Also state that the registered manifest hashes remain the trust anchor for provider downloads\. If the hash check was removed unintentionally, restore it\. The backend code is out of scope here, so this is unconfirmed\.

findings.detail: In `publish_revision_only` mode, the payload at lines 190-192 contains only `version` and `hugging_face_artifact`. The `promote` input is dropped, and the input description says the mode will 'Publish and promote'. An operator who sets `promote=false` together with `publish_revision_only=true` expecting a staged-only publish therefore sends a request that, per the documentation, promotes the revision. Promotion changes the manifest providers download and verify (A-004, T-027, T-012) and is meant to need specific approval. The workflow has no environment or approval gate; a single publishing key is enough, and the script does not validate that `version` matches a reviewed upload. Fix: reject `promote=false` when `publish_revision_only` is set, or send an explicit promote flag and let the backend honour it. Put the job behind a protected GitHub environment with required reviewers. Also require a non-null pinned `hugging_face_artifact` or document what null does to an existing pinned source.
findings.title: Revision-only mode ignores the `promote` input and always promotes

findings.detail: The runbook previously said HandleRegisterModel verified that every listed file exists with the declared size and hash. It now says the handler only validates identity and declared inventory and checks listed file sizes, and that providers verify hashes at download time. Step 1 also lets operators skip upload and reuse an already-published manifest. A mismatched, corrupted or substituted object under the CDN prefix could then be registered and promoted with no coordinator-side content check. The alias fan-out would push that build to the fleet, and each provider's hard-swap is the only point where the bytes are checked. The trigger is a publishing mistake or CDN/R2 tampering. The impact is fleet-wide failed prefetches and retry load, or a stale or incorrect weightHash in the catalog. A malicious provider could also exploit a weak catalog hash to pass the weight-hash routing gate (T-027, T-012, SEC-007). The threat model and A-004 notes still describe coordinator weight-hash verification and have not been updated. The fix is to update the threat model, or restore hash verification at registration. Otherwise the runbook should require a pre-register hash audit and a single-provider canary before any promote or alias flip.
findings.title: Registration no longer documented as verifying file hashes; integrity rests on provider-side checks
